column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

**Top Tc samples in the data (using only allowed elements):**

| Composition | Tc (K) | Family |
|---|---|---|
| Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 | 132.0 | Hg-cuprate (Hg not allowed) |
| Ba2Ca2Cu3O | 126.0 | cuprate |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O | 120.2 | Tl-cuprate (Tl not allowed) |
| Bi2Sr2Ca1Cu2O10 | 110.0 | Bi-2212/2223 |
| Bi1.4Pb0.5Sb0.1Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 109.0 | (Bi,Pb)-2223 |
| Cu4.5V0.5Sr2Ca1O | 107.0 | cuprate |
| Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 105.7 | Bi-2223 |

The clear pattern: **high-Tc region = layered cuprates** rich in Cu–O planes with alkaline-earth spacers (Sr/Ba/Ca) and a Bi/Pb charge-reservoir layer. Since Hg, Tl, and H (185 K H2S is an isolated outlier and H isn't a design variable) are unavailable, the accessible optimum is the **(Bi,Pb)–(Sr,Ba)–Ca–Cu–O "2223" family**, which occupies a *broad plateau* (~90–120 K) in composition space:

- Bi 1.2–2.1, Pb 0–0.8, Sr+Ba ≈ 2, Ca 1–2, Cu 2–3, O ~8–10 all give Tc ≥ 89 K.
- Small perturbations (±5 %) in any one fraction keep the composition inside this dense cloud of ≥ 90 K samples — a robust, flat optimum, unlike the single-point Ba2Ca2Cu3O (126 K) sample whose O fraction (0.125) is anomalously low and isolated.

**Proposed compound:** Bi₁.₅Pb₀.₅Sr₁.₆Ba₀.₄Ca₂Cu₃O₁₀ (Pb-stabilized 2223 with mixed Sr/Ba, emulating the 120 K structure). Total atoms = 19, giving fractions:

- O = 10/19 = 0.526316
- Cu = 3/19 = 0.157895
- Ca = 2/19 = 0.105263
- Sr = 1.6/19 = 0.084211
- Bi = 1.5/19 = 0.078947
- Pb = 0.5/19 = 0.026316
- Ba = 0.4/19 = 0.021053

All within observed ranges. A ±5 % shift in any single fraction (e.g., O: 0.50–0.55, Cu: 0.15–0.166) stays fully within the composition envelope of the many 89–110 K training samples, so Tc will not collapse.

**Final: O=0.526316, Cu=0.157895, Ba=0.021053, Sr=0.084211, Y=0, Ca=0.105263, La=0, Bi=0.078947, Fe=0, Nb=0, C=0, Pr=0, As=0, B=0, Pb=0.026316, Ce=0, Mo=0, V=0, Zn=0, Ni=0**
